scope: Audit of HSConfig operator UX and skill alignment on branch codex/no-silent-default-only-closure at commit eb411b4cb15c9df668ea8fd4e7ac29df8b6b1840. The review covers the installed Codex hsconfig skill at C:/Users/darbo/.codex/skills/hsconfig/SKILL.md, the repo skill under .agents/skills/hsconfig, README.md, docs/operator/README.md, docs/operator/guide-research-policy.md, hsconfig configure, hsconfig apply, apply_gate, runtime_apply, operator_summary, policy-backed autonomous Mulligan behavior, default-only visibility, and Darkbishop Benedictus effect-not-mulligan guardrails.
verified_strengths: The installed hsconfig skill is synchronized with the repository skill. scripts/sync_installed_skill.py --check reported that C:/Users/darbo/.codex/skills/hsconfig is in sync, so the operator-facing Codex skill currently communicates the same normal path and contract language as the repo-owned skill.

The normal operator path is clear and consistent across README.md, docs/operator/README.md, .agents/skills/hsconfig/SKILL.md, and the installed skill: use hsconfig configure for ordinary deck-to-package operation, open reports/operator_summary.json first, and use lower-level source-manifest -> draft-source-documents -> research-deck -> prepare -> validate -> apply only for inspected stages.

The configure command implements the documented deck-in workflow. src/hsconfig/commands/configure.py creates 01_manifest, 02_source_documents, 03_research, and 04_package stages, runs source_manifest_payload, optional draft_source_documents_payload, research_deck_payload with auto_research_fallback, prepare_package_payload, validate_payload, and only calls apply_payload when --apply is explicitly set.

The apply workflow does not require manual approval for source-depth warnings. src/hsconfig/apply_gate.py allows load_safe_apply whenever reports/operator_summary.json has technical_status=VALID_PACKAGE and the package passes structural/runtime-file checks; it does not block on SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG, source evidence warnings, guide-strength gaps, source_to_runtime_explainability, source_contract_audit, config_usefulness, or default-only diagnostics.

Operator guidance matches the no-manual-approval contract. src/hsconfig/operator_guidance.py returns safe_to_apply=true, normal_next_step=apply_with_warnings, normal_next_command=hsconfig apply --package <package> --runtime-root <runtime-root> --json, and requires_expert_flag=false for load_safe_apply packages with warnings.

Runtime apply is still guarded. src/hsconfig/runtime_apply.py revalidates the package, resolves evaluate_apply_gate(package), rejects mismatched or forged caller gates, verifies that the allowed gate points to the same package's reports/operator_summary.json, creates or verifies fake apply receipts, and only then mutates the runtime root.

The docs and skill correctly distinguish technical validity from source strength. VALID_PACKAGE, runtime_load_safe, runtime_apply_mode=load_safe_apply, runtime_apply_allowed, and apply_policy decide load-safe runtime write posture; SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG, STATIC_SEMANTICS_USABLE, VALID_BUT_NOT_GUIDE_STRONG, source_claim_quality_summary, and guide_strength_summary remain confidence and source-depth labels.

No-silent-default-only language is present in both operator docs and skill text. docs/operator/README.md and docs/operator/guide-research-policy.md instruct operators to inspect mulligan_policy_status, surface_status_ledger, default_only_runtime_surfaces, default_only_runtime_surface_details, and source_to_runtime_explainability when a package is thin, while keeping operator_summary.json as the only normal apply authority.

The surface status ledger gives a compact operator view without becoming a gate. operator_summary builds surface_status_ledger rows with statuses such as source_backed, policy_backed, static_semantics_backed, warning_only, suppressed_with_reason, or default_only, and the docs explicitly say ledger rows are diagnostic-only with apply_blocking=false.

Policy-backed autonomous Mulligan prevents default-only Mulligan output without pretending to be source-backed evidence. docs/operator/guide-research-policy.md and .agents/skills/hsconfig/SKILL.md state that policy_backed_autonomous_mulligan is weaker than guide evidence, does not promote SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG, and must stay visible in operator_summary and mulligan_plan_report.

The autonomous Mulligan implementation follows that contract. src/hsconfig/autonomous_mulligan_policy.py selects at most a small low-curve set from role/lane signals, marks rules with confidence=policy_backed and source_type=policy_backed_autonomous_mulligan, records suppressed cards, and excludes start-of-game non-hand effects before fallback selection.

Darkbishop Benedictus is guarded at the UX, policy, implementation, and test layers. The installed skill, repo skill, operator README, guide research policy, source surface gate tests, source evidence verifier tests, autonomous Mulligan tests, and ShadowPriest E2E tests all preserve hero-power transform / Mind Spike semantics while keeping SW_448 out of Mulligan.json unless explicit opening-hand source text exists.

The source research policy rejects false lowering through a simple operator rule: claim_kind, source_contract_matrix, surface gate, and builder/router output decide runtime emission; guide importance, archetype value, effect relevance, runtime_block hints, and policy_lane alone do not bypass that chain.

Default-only and closure freshness diagnostics are visible but non-blocking. docs/operator/guide-research-policy.md says closure_schema_current, cards_missing_closure, closure lane counts, default_only_runtime_surface_details, and source_to_runtime_explainability are diagnostic-only and must not become a second runtime-write gate.

correctness_gaps: Deck-in autonomy does not mean every package is source-backed strong. A deck with no current guide evidence can still produce a technically valid package through static semantics and policy-backed Mulligan, but that output must remain labeled as policy-backed, static-semantics-backed, or valid but not guide-strong.

Policy-backed Mulligan is a usefulness fallback, not strategic proof. The fallback can prevent an empty/default-only Mulligan.json by choosing low-curve anchors, but it cannot prove matchup-specific or archetype-specific optimal keeps without guide evidence.

The fallback includes a lowest-curve anchor path when role signals are sparse. That preserves no-block operation, but it is the weakest policy lane and should remain visible through policy_reason and policy_lanes rather than being described as source-backed.

The apply gate intentionally trusts operator_summary technical_status after independently checking package structure, required runtime files, generated-file parity, optional legacy surfaces, and runtime JSON validity. It does not recompute source-depth, default-only, or semantic richness, so stale or low-quality diagnostics must be caught by generation and tests rather than by runtime write permission.

source_informed_apply_readiness can be blocked by source_evidence_warnings or other semantic blockers while runtime apply remains allowed. That split is correct, but future UI text must keep distinguishing source-informed strong handoff from load-safe apply.

The current evidence is representative and regression-backed, not a mathematical proof for every possible future Wild deck, expansion mechanic, or guide wording pattern. Future claim kinds, runtime surfaces, or mechanics still need the same docs, source-contract matrix, surface-gate, builder/router, and tests updated together.

The operator docs are accurate but dense. The density protects against common misunderstandings, but it can make normal users over-read diagnostic reports as required approval steps if summaries or automations do not foreground the single next command.
default_only_gaps: surface_status_ledger only covers surfaces represented through config_usefulness and related summaries. If a future runtime surface is added without extending those projections, the operator may not get the same no-silent-default-only visibility for that surface.

default_only_runtime_surfaces is still surface-level while source_to_runtime_explainability is card-level. This is acceptable now, but future multi-surface default-only cases should keep surface-specific card examples and first missing links synchronized.

Policy-backed Mulligan changes the Mulligan surface from default_only to policy_backed. That is the intended autonomy improvement, but it means operators must continue to see that policy-backed is weaker than source-backed and does not imply SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG.

A technically valid package can still be load_safe_but_thin. The docs expose this through config_usefulness and next_report_to_open, but automated wrappers around hsconfig configure should surface default_only_runtime_surfaces, mulligan_policy_status, and surface_status_ledger instead of only reporting status=OK.

The ledger points compactly to reports/operator_summary.json for some diagnostic follow-up. Operators still need the docs' instruction to inspect default_only_runtime_surface_details and reports/source_to_runtime_explainability.json when a surface is default-only or thin.
slimness_gaps: The same core operator contract is repeated across README.md, docs/operator/README.md, docs/operator/guide-research-policy.md, .agents/skills/hsconfig/SKILL.md, .agents/skills/hsconfig/references/workflow.md, and the installed skill. This repetition is currently useful for alignment, but future changes must keep sync checks and focused docs tests in place to avoid drift.

The operator UX now has several adjacent diagnostic terms: mulligan_policy_status, surface_status_ledger, default_only_runtime_surfaces, default_only_runtime_surface_details, source_to_runtime_explainability_summary, config_usefulness, source_claim_quality_summary, guide_strength_summary, and no_block_failure_mode_summary. They are coherent today, but new UX fields should be added only if they replace or simplify an existing operator decision.

The guide research policy is the right place for claim-kind and false-lowering rules, but it is long enough that the normal path should continue to be summarized in docs/operator/README.md and the skill rather than forcing operators to read the full policy before every configure run.

Do not solve operator uncertainty by adding a manual approval layer. The current slimness win is that one gate answers apply permission and diagnostics answer quality debt; approval flags or second gates would duplicate authority.

Do not add named-card exceptions for Darkbishop-style behavior. The durable rule is start-of-game and other non-hand effects are not opening-hand keeps unless current source text explicitly says opening hand or mulligan.
autonomy_gaps: hsconfig configure is autonomous for valid deck input, but fully source-backed output still depends on available current guide evidence or provided source evidence. When source depth is thin, autonomy relies on static semantics and policy-backed fallbacks rather than source-backed strength.

The installed skill tells Codex to use current guide research, but the normal configure path can also run without supplied source documents. That is correct for any-deck no-block operation, but outputs must keep source-backed versus policy-backed labels prominent.

Warnings do not block apply, so an unattended configure --apply path can write a load-safe but weak package. This is intended, but completion summaries should report warnings and policy/default-only status so quality debt is not silently ignored.

Skill sync is currently verified by a script and tests, not by the runtime itself. If the installed skill drifts after a repo change, Codex UX can become stale until scripts/sync_installed_skill.py --check or tests/test_skill_sync.py runs.

Future source-depth warning categories could accidentally sound like approval requirements. The docs and operator_guidance should keep warning categories framed as follow-up work unless technical_status is invalid or the apply gate blocks structurally.

The existing focused tests prove the Darkbishop canary and representative configure/apply behavior, but future operator UI changes should also test the exact generated words for apply_with_warnings and requires_expert_flag=false to prevent manual-approval drift.
guardrails_to_keep: Keep hsconfig configure as the normal one-command operator path, with source-manifest, draft-source-documents, research-deck, prepare, validate, and apply reserved as inspected or lower-level stages.
Keep reports/operator_summary.json as the first report to open and the only normal apply authority.
Keep runtime writes limited to hsconfig apply and hsconfig configure --apply, with runtime_apply re-evaluating evaluate_apply_gate before any mutation.

Keep evaluate_apply_gate focused on technical_status=VALID_PACKAGE plus package structure, input_manifest, GlobalValues.json, Mulligan.json, generated-file parity, valid runtime JSON, and absence of normal-path Presume.json or Concede.json.
Keep ALLOWED_WITH_WARNINGS and READY_TO_APPLY_WITH_WARNINGS as runtime-write-capable states when technical_status=VALID_PACKAGE and runtime_apply_mode=load_safe_apply.

Keep source-depth warnings, default-only details, source_contract_audit.json, source_to_runtime_explainability.json, closure freshness, contract_spine_rows, mechanic visibility, and source_claim_quality_summary diagnostic-only.

Keep policy_backed_autonomous_mulligan visible, limited, and weaker than guide evidence; it must not promote SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG and must not override explicit, suppressed, quarantined, or contradictory Mulligan source intent.

Keep non-hand start-of-game, deckbuilding, highlander, odd/even, and hero-power-transform effects out of policy-backed and source-backed opening-hand keeps unless source text explicitly states opening-hand mulligan intent.

Keep Darkbishop Benedictus / SW_448 as the regression canary: preserve the Shadowform / Mind Spike effect on supported CardID behavior surfaces while proving SW_448 is absent from Mulligan.json without explicit opening-hand source text.
Keep scripts/sync_installed_skill.py --check and tests/test_skill_sync.py as release guardrails for installed skill alignment.

Keep tests/test_docs_active_path.py, tests/test_operator_docs_contract_policy.py, tests/test_configure_cli.py, tests/test_apply_gate.py, tests/test_autonomous_mulligan_policy.py, tests/test_surface_authority_split.py, tests/test_source_evidence_verifier.py, and tests/test_shadowpriest_depth_e2e.py in the focused operator UX guardrail set.
recommended_next_design: Keep the current operator design. The right UX is deck in through hsconfig configure, source-backed when evidence exists, policy-backed or static-semantics-backed when source evidence is thin, visible no-silent-default-only diagnostics, and guarded runtime apply from operator_summary technical validity without manual approval for source-depth warnings. The next design move should be subtractive polish only: preserve the existing gate and sync checks, keep the normal path short in README/skill text, and avoid adding a second apply gate, manual approval flag, or named-card exception system.
